correctness.rationale: After translating \(A\) to contain zero, nonnegativity and the convolution equation imply \(h(d)=0\) for every nonzero \(d\in A-A\). Thus every candidate satisfies an exact integer linear system. A fresh independent exhaustive replay generated all \(46\) \(\mathrm{GL}(4,2)\)-orbits of the \(32768\) normalized subsets; exactly \(9\) orbit representatives tile by the difference-set criterion, while each of the other \(37\) representatives has augmented rational rank exactly one above coefficient rank in the necessary weak-tiling system. The replay independently recovered normalized counts \(1,15,455,1395,1\). This exhaustive finite certificate establishes the finite theorem; no floating-point feasibility test is involved.
correctness.risk: The result is dimension-specific and does not address unnormalized weak complements.

originality.rationale: The full open primary paper was inspected closely because Proposition 3.1 is printed as saying non-pd-flatness for \(d\ge4\). Its surrounding text explicitly restricts the known non-tiling spectral counterexamples to odd primes, and the proof of the \(d\ge4\) clause uses exactly those odd-prime examples. Thus the printed proposition does not supply a valid \(p=2,d=4\) obstruction. The submitted exact census resolves that binary case and is stronger than pd-flatness because it drops Fourier positivity. Later weak-tiling counterexamples concern different ambient settings/notions. Resultary found no prior binary four-dimensional classification.

final_claim: In \(\mathbb F_2^4\), every nonempty set admitting a nonnegative weak complement \(h\) with \(h(0)=1\) and \(1_A*h=1\) is a translational tile. Consequently \(\mathbb F_2^4\) is pd-flat; the normalized census has \(46\) linear-equivalence classes, exactly \(9\) tiling classes, and tiling-set counts \(1,15,455,1395,1\) at sizes \(1,2,4,8,16\).
limitations: The normalization \(h(0)=1\) is essential to the statement.
No conclusion for binary dimensions at least five.
